svg.title: The dispatch digest as a pipeline of collections
svg.desc: Data flows from left to right, with the numbers of the lesson sample. List rows returns 8 raw work orders: raw values plus formatted value annotations. The Select action named Rows maps each one to seven flat properties: Number, Site, Subcontractor, Status, When in Amman time, Urgent and Flag; the array still has 8 items. From Rows, five Filter array actions run side by side: Needs attention keeps 3 rows, namely WO-1001 overdue, WO-1003 rejected and WO-1004 unplanned; Overdue keeps 1; Unplanned 1; Rejected 1; Next 24 h keeps 3. The function length applied to each filter gives the numbers in the subject: Dispatch digest Tue 6 Oct: 1 overdue, 1 unplanned, 1 rejected, 3 in the next 24 h (8 open). Create HTML table turns the 3 attention rows into a table; a Compose chooses between the table and the sentence All clear; one Send an email action sends the result. There is no loop and no variable: 12 actions whatever the number of work orders. The old flow had 47 actions, a loop with five conditions and six variables, and took four minutes.
svg.text: Map, filter, count, format: collections in, collections out
